issues.title: Missing ConfigureAwait(false) on Task.Yield
issues.description: The rule requires all await expressions in library code (non-test, non-sample projects) to use .ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid capturing the synchronization context, but the await Task.Yield() expression at line 291 omits it.
issues.rule_name: Async Methods Must Use ConfigureAwait(false) in Library Code

issues.title: Logout validation incorrectly rejects valid logout requests when HistoryEntryState is null
issues.description: The sign-out validation logic was modified to remove the null check for Navigation.HistoryEntryState before calling ValidateSignOutRequestState(). This causes ValidateSignOutRequestState() to return false when HistoryEntryState is null (since GetCachedNavigationState() returns null), which incorrectly redirects users to the logout failure page even for legitimate logout operations. The original code correctly allowed logout when HistoryEntryState is null by using the condition 'HistoryEntryState != null && !ValidateSignOutRequestState()', which only validated if state existed. This breaks backward compatibility with logout flows that don't use history state.

issues.title: Missing null check for InteractiveRequestUrl causes potential null reference in navigation
issues.description: The Redirect() method condition was changed from checking both InteractionOptions and InteractiveRequestUrl to only checking InteractionOptions. This creates a bug where if InteractionOptions is not null but InteractiveRequestUrl is null, the code will call NavigateToLogin with a null URL parameter at line 40. The NavigateToLogin method expects a non-null URL, so this will cause a null reference exception or navigation failure. The original PR properly validated both properties before choosing the navigation method.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #62755 - [Blazor] Remove obsolete APIs from Components

structured_output.summary:
The PR removes a set of APIs previously marked [Obsolete] across Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components, Forms, Web, WebAssembly and WebAssembly.Authentication: Router.PreferExactMatches, the RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions class, the WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions class, SignOutSessionStateManager, several AccessTokenResult/RemoteAuthenticationService constructors and members, and the JSInteropMethods/InternalCalls entries. Removals are recorded as *REMOVED* lines in the Unshipped PublicAPI files, and I found no remaining in-repo callers of the removed symbols. The removals themselves are mechanically sound and consistent with the stated policy.

The PR also contains behavior changes that go beyond deletion. The most important is in RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut: the old backcompat branch was collapsed into a single `if (!ValidateSignOutRequestState())`, so a logout with a null HistoryEntryState now always fails. The PR description says the opposite ("only fail validation when state exists but is invalid"). Two other changes are unexplained: an added `await Task.Yield()` with a comment that does not match what it does, and a rewritten AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect that can now pass a null URL to NavigateToLogin. The PR also deletes a still-valid logout-failure test instead of keeping it, which removes coverage of the invalid-state path it was guarding.

Overall the API removals look right, but the authentication logout changes need to be fixed or justified before merge."
structured_output.verdictRationale: The API deletions are clean and have no leftover callers. The blocking issues are in the authentication code. ProcessLogOut now rejects every logout that lacks history state, which contradicts the PR description and drops the backcompat fallback without a test. The Task.Yield addition is unexplained with a misleading comment. The Redirect() rewrite removes a null guard. A passing logout-failure test was deleted rather than kept. None of these are exotic, but each changes sign-out or redirect behavior, so they should be resolved first.

architecture.overview:
Blazor's Components library exposes public APIs across several packages: Components (Router), Forms (EditContextDataAnnotationsExtensions), Web (WebRenderer, event callback factory extensions, file streams), WebAssembly (JSInteropMethods, InternalCalls) and WebAssembly.Authentication (RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore, RemoteAuthenticationService, AccessTokenResult, AccessTokenNotAvailableException, SignOutSessionStateManager). Each package tracks its public surface in PublicAPI.Shipped.txt and PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, and removals are recorded as *REMOVED* lines in the Unshipped file. Obsolete members were kept for backwards compatibility.

This PR deletes those obsolete members. In the WebAssembly authentication flow it also changes runtime logic: the sign-out path in RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore no longer consults the separately-registered SignOutSessionStateManager (session storage). It now relies only on the InteractiveRequestOptions carried in history state, and AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect no longer falls back to a RedirectUrl property.
steps: Start at the public surface: each package's PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt now lists *REMOVED* entries for the deleted types and members, and the Shipped files are unchanged, which matches the API baseline policy.

Components, Forms, and Web: Router.PreferExactMatches, EditContextDataAnnotationsExtensions.AddDataAnnotationsValidation and EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(EditContext), the RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions class, the WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions class, and the WebRenderer.RendererId init accessor are all removed. These are pure deletions, and no in-repo callers remain.

WebAssembly: JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool) and the InternalCalls.InvokeJS interop declaration are removed. The InternalCalls comment says that declaration exists for Mono driver backcompat, so this deletion needs runtime-side confirmation.

WebAssembly.Authentication, the core logic change: RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut drops the SignOutManager fallback. It now calls ValidateSignOutRequestState() unconditionally, which returns false when HistoryEntryState is null. It also adds an unexplained Task.Yield() before the authentication-state check.

AccessTokenResult and AccessTokenNotAvailableException: the obsolete 3-argument constructor and RedirectUrl property are removed. Redirect() now navigates with InteractiveRequestUrl directly, but its null guard on InteractiveRequestUrl was removed, so a null URL can reach NavigateToLogin.

Tests: the obsolete-API tests and the TestSignOutSessionStateManager helper are removed. The deleted logout-failure test covered a non-null, invalid-state branch that still exists, so that coverage is lost rather than migrated.

findings.title: Logout with null history state now always fails, contradicting the PR description
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` (around lines 281-285) now rejects any logout where `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` is false, which includes a null `Navigation.HistoryEntryState`. The PR description says null state should only fail when state exists but is invalid. Decide which behavior is correct. If null-state rejection is intended, update the PR description to say so and add a test for a null-state logout that asserts a redirect to LogOutFailedPath. If not, restore the null-state allowance in the condition. Match the style of the existing `ValidateSignOutRequestState` and `GetCachedNavigationState` helpers.

findings.title: Unexplained Task.Yield() with a misleading comment added to sign-out
findings.body:
The PR adds `await Task.Yield();` in `ProcessLogOut` with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out". `Task.Yield()` does not authenticate anything. It only yields the current continuation. The next line already calls `GetAuthenticationStateAsync()` and checks `IsAuthenticated`.

This is behavior that doesn't belong in a PR whose stated purpose is removing obsolete APIs. It changes scheduling in the logout path with no test or rationale. A reviewer reading the comment would believe a real guard was added.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs" lines="288-292"}

If the yield is needed to work around a render or dispatcher ordering issue, say so in the comment and add a test that depends on it. If it isn't needed, remove it.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` has an `await Task.Yield();` added around line 291 with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out". Task.Yield does not authenticate, and the comment is wrong. Either remove the yield and the comment, since the following `GetAuthenticationStateAsync()` check already handles authentication, or, if a real scheduling reason exists, replace the comment with that reason and add a test that depends on it. This PR is about removing obsolete APIs, so keep unrelated behavior changes out of it.

findings.title: Redirect() can pass a null URL to NavigateToLogin and NavigateTo
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs`, `Redirect()` (around lines 38-45) was changed to drop the `InteractiveRequestUrl != null` check, and the else branch uses `InteractiveRequestUrl!`. A result with non-null options and a null URL now calls `NavigateToLogin` with null. Restore a null check on `InteractiveRequestUrl` before navigating. Choose a clear failure mode for the case where no URL is available. Don't rely on the null-forgiving operator. Add a test in `AuthorizationMessageHandlerTests.cs` or a new test file that covers a RequiresRedirect result with a null URL.

findings.title: Deleted logout-failure test removes coverage of a path that still exists
findings.body:
The PR deletes `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState`. It was justified as obsolete-API cleanup, but the test uses an `InteractionType.SignIn` state. That is a non-null, invalid state, and that branch still exists in `ValidateSignOutRequestState()`. The test would still pass against the new code.

The deletion removes the only test for the invalid-state logout failure. No test replaces it, and there is still no test for the null-state path the PR changed.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs" lines="370-374"}

Restore the test, drop only the `SignOutManager` setup, and add a null-state case so the new behavior is covered.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs`, the test `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState` was deleted (around the hunk at lines 370-374). It covered a non-null SignIn state that is still rejected by the current `ValidateSignOutRequestState()`, so the test still applies. Restore it without the `SignOutManager` / `TestSignOutSessionStateManager` setup, which was the only part tied to the removed API. Also add a test for a logout with a null HistoryEntryState, asserting the redirect to `logout-failed` as the new behavior requires. Follow the existing `CreateAuthenticationManager` and `TestNavigationManager` patterns in that file.

findings.title: Removing InternalCalls.InvokeJS may break older Mono runtimes
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/JSInterop/src/InternalCalls.cs`, the `InvokeJS<T0,T1,T2,TRes>` InternalCall was removed. Its comment says it exists for backwards compatibility with entries in Mono's `driver.c`. Confirm with the WebAssembly runtime owners that no supported Mono runtime version still resolves this export. If one does, restore the declaration or document the supported runtime boundary in the PR description. Keep the existing comment's cross-reference accurate.

findings.title: Removed public APIs are reflected correctly in the PublicAPI baselines
findings.body:
Each deleted public member has a matching `*REMOVED*` line in the appropriate `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, and the Shipped files are untouched. That is exactly what the analyzer workflow expects. The `~static` marker on the `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool)` entry also matches the existing `~` form in `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt`.

I found no remaining in-repo references to the removed symbols: `PreferExactMatches`, `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, `SignOutSessionStateManager`, `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, and `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions`. The only remaining `PreferExactMatches` is a separate property on a test-only `CustomRouter`.

findings.title: WebRenderer.RendererId is now read-only with no behavior change
findings.body: The `init` accessor was a no-op, so dropping it doesn't change any behavior. `_rendererId` is still assigned in the constructor from `GetWebRendererId()`, and the getter is unchanged. Any subclass that used the `init` setter now fails at compile time, which is what the removal is meant to do.
